newsitem.title: UK: Jardine Fleming confirms Smith, Thomas to retire.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming confirms Smith, Thomas to retire.

text.p: Investment bank Jardine Fleming Holdings Ltd confirmed on Thursday that Alan Smith is to retire as its chairman.
In a statement the group also said that Robert Thomas, who recently lost his registration with the British investment watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, will also retire.
A spokesman declined to say if the announcements were linked to a recent scandal in Hong Kong and London over the company's fund management practices.

Jardine Fleming, jointly owned by Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd and Robert Fleming Group, also announced the creation of a new supervisory board. The board will be headed by Alasdair Morrison, managing director of Jardine Matheson.

Jardine Fleming said it would appoint James Bruce, currently head of global capital markets in London, to the new post of country head for Hong Kong and China, with responsibility for management of all the group's activities.
It said Patrick Sun would move from rival SBC Warburg to head the group's investment banking operations in China and Hong Kong.
Jardine Fleming said the new two-tier board structure would ensure the involvement of its key shareholders at the highest level "with executive responsibility for Jardine Fleming."
"We see the board as institutionalising the relationship. We think it crystallises the relationship and makes clear the partners' commitment to Jardine Fleming's future," the spokesman said.
The supervisory board will be made up of four representatives of Jardine Matheson, four from Robert Fleming and two from Jardine Fleming.

The spokesman declined to link Alan Smith's departure with recent revelations of irregular trading practices at Jardine Fleming, which is involved in asset management, securities and investment banking.
"Now the restructuring is in place he believes it is the right time to retire," the spokesman said.

Jardine Fleming was fined and reprimanded by British and Hong Kong watchdogs last month after an investigation revealed that Colin Armstrong, a former senior fund manager and director of Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM), delayed processing transactions to await subsequent price changes.
Smith has been with Jardine Fleming for 24 years, including three as chairman and three as managing director.
Thomas, who resigned as managing director of JFIM and Jardine Fleming Asset Management last month, spent 30 years with the company.
